target_material: indium oxide (In2O3) and indium-doped zinc oxide (IZO)
summary: The study investigates the growth of indium oxide (In2O3) and indium-doped zinc oxide (IZO) thin films using thermal atomic layer deposition (Th-ALD). The films were deposited using DMLDMIn as the In2O3 precursor and diethylzinc as the ZnO precursor, with DI water as the reactant. The IZO films were deposited using the supercycle method, and the doping concentration was controlled by varying the In2O3/ZnO cycle ratio. The films were analyzed for microstructural properties, chemical composition, and electrical characteristics, including resistivity, carrier concentration, and mobility. The lowest resistivity of 6.15 × 10−2 Ω·cm was achieved for the IZO film grown at 300 °C.
evidence: We investigated the growth of indium oxide (In2O3) and indium-doped zinc oxide (In-doped ZnO, IZO) thin films synthesized using thermal atomic layer deposition with dimethylamino-dimethylindium as the precursor, while varying the In2O3/ZnO ratio. The IZO films were deposited using the supercycle method, and the doping concentration of these films was controlled by changing the In2O3/ZnO cycle ratio. The microstructural properties and chemical compositions of the films were analyzed using X-ray diffraction analysis and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. Further, the electrical properties of the IZO films, including their carrier concentration, mobility, and resistivity, were investigated through Hall measurements. The lowest resistivity (6.15 × 10−2 Ω ·cm) was exhibited by the IZO film. The highest carrier concentration and mobility exhibited by the IZO films grown at 300 °C were 4.4 × 1018 cm−3 and 28.7 cm2/V·s, respectively.
